constraints: Decision (user, verbatim): the workflow PreToolUse hook allows, without a prompt, an inline script the root writes in which every agent() call uses a holyagent specialist (agentType holyagent:*); a script with any other agent type, a scriptPath or a resume keeps the normal permission flow.

blockers:
- BLOCKER (behavior, false allow): packages/runtime/src/cli/hook.ts:347-382 (UNSAFE_NAMES, onlyOurAgents). The denylist matches identifier tokens only, so a string or template subscript reaches the same names. I ran the hook on `await agent('p',{agentType:'holyagent:worker-implementation'}); [].at['constructor']('return agent("p",{agentType:"general-purpose"})')()` and got ALLOW. The template form [].at[`constructor`] is also ALLOW. A script that runs a non-holyagent agent() or other code therefore skips the prompt, which the user's decision forbids (every agent() call a holyagent specialist, else the normal flow). docs/hooks.md says the lexer refuses 'the other names that could reach agent or run code the lexer does not see', and the hook runs with onFailure block on that premise. Probes `await Bun.$`echo hi`` and `await fetch('http://x')` also ALLOW; only the sandbox decides whether Bun and fetch exist there, and I could not run the Workflow sandbox. The script does not need to reach Function by name. Fix: refuse any computed member access (`[` directly after an ident, `)` or `]`; array literals after an operator are fine) and refuse any string or template token equal to a UNSAFE_NAMES entry. Optionally invert to an allowlist of globals. Add a test in packages/integrations/claude/tests/hooks.test.ts beside the 'Function constructor' case at line 293; no existing test covers a subscripted name.
notes:
- code-review claim, confirmed and treated as the blocker: constructor/Bun/fetch false allows (hook.ts:347-382).
- code-review claim, optional: hook.ts:327 startsOurAgent checks only the agentType key. `{agentType:'holyagent:worker-implementation', permissionMode:'bypassPermissions'}`, `isolation:'worktree'` and `"__proto__":{...}` all ALLOW (verified). The workflow-authoring agent() option list has no permissionMode, so only an unknown key is passed through, and the agentType itself stays a literal holyagent specialist. Restricting keys to model/effort/label/phase/agentType, and refusing a quoted __proto__ key, would be tighter.
- code-review claim, optional: hook.ts:186 the template/code tokenizer recurses without a bound. A script with 20000 nested `${` substitutions throws RangeError (verified). The run callback is synchronous inside Effect.flatMap, so it becomes a defect, not the documented 'no decision'. It fails closed under onFailure block but contradicts docs/hooks.md, which says unreadable code gets the normal permission flow. Add a depth cap that returns undefined. The 20000-line script with comments took 31 ms, so the source.slice cost is not a practical concern.
- code-review claim, rejected as stated: `else agent(...)` is refused but `else await agent(...)` is ALLOW (verified), so only a bare `else agent(` or `yield agent(` over-refuses. That fails closed and is optional. Over-refusal of an `agent:` object key does exist (agentKey probe returns nothing): the documented entry shape {id, agent, model, effort, prompt} inlined in a script gets a prompt. Optional, but it touches the stated goal of a prompt-free happy path. Scripts take entries from `args`, so the usual script should not hit it.
- code-review claim, optional: INLINE_INPUTS (hook.ts:400) is only script and args. A Workflow call carrying description or title falls back to the normal flow. Fails closed. I could not verify the real Workflow tool schema.
- code-review claim, optional: assignment.ts:247 --report-json help still says it takes a JSON report from an agent() given a schema, and the notes now say to use it only for a JSON report object. It is consistent enough, not a blocker.
- code-review claim, optional: closeOf, balanced and splitTop are three bracket walkers (hook.ts, around 205-260). A future change to one could leave the others inconsistent. Maintainability only.
- code-review claim, optional: eight .holyagent/intents/.../assignments/*.json state files are committed in this range. They match the repo's own state convention and .prettierignore changes, but they add churn and local paths. The root should confirm that the state commits in this range are intended.
- Lexer cases that held in my probes, all refused: aliasing, `(0,agent)`, `agent?.(`, tagged template, `new agent`, a duplicate agentType key, an `__proto__:` shorthand key, regex literals, reassigning `agent`, parameter shadowing and unbalanced brackets. The deep-paren script was refused without a crash. `await agent(...)` inside an arrow body is allowed, which is fine since the call itself is vetted.
- Plan and help: PLAN_NOTES and the plan output are consistent with the new SHAPES. The workflow name field is gone, and no prebuilt workflow remains in src (grep finds names only in tests as negations and in .holyagent state). I did not run `plan --help` interactively; I read the diff, and the tests in cli.test.ts and directive.test.ts passed under verify.
- Read only, not run: how the real Workflow sandbox treats `Function`, `Bun` and `fetch`. The tree was static (HEAD ce0bd66), with no moving-tree concern.
